ladder.improve_note: past an advance's home level its figure gets half as much better again per level (times 1.5 where higher is better, divided by 1.5 where lower is), until it meets the next cited allowed or ceiling mark, then stops

balances.name: Energy pays for the exhaust
balances.near_c: gamma - 1 <= fuel_j_per_kg / c^2 for the exhaust's speed (the relativistic form)
balances.catches: a chemical fuel with a torch's exhaust speed

balances.name: Jet power
balances.catches: thrust and exhaust speed set apart that need more power than the ship makes

balances.name: Energy in, energy out
balances.catches: waste heat set to nothing while the plant's efficiency says otherwise

balances.name: Momentum
balances.relation: thrust_n = mdot_kg_s * exhaust_km_s * 1000, or thrust_n <= plant_w * unthrown_n_per_w for light alone
balances.catches: thrust with nothing thrown and no stated partner

balances.name: Heat flows downhill
balances.relation: radiator_k <= waste_heat_k, unless a heat pump is paid for: pump_w >= q_w * (t_hot_k - t_cold_k) / t_cold_k, and pump_w is shed too
balances.catches: a hot radiator cooling a cool room for free

J. 2005, Realizing '2001: A Space Odyssey': piloted spherical torus nuclear fusion propulsion, NASA/TM-2005-213559 (AIAA 2001-3805): D-He3, specific impulse 35,435 s (Jupiter mission), jet power 4,830 MW, specific power 8.62 kW/kg

sources.openstax-up3: Ling, S. J., Sanny, J. and Moebs, W. 2016, University Physics volume 3, OpenStax, section 10.5: fission of 1.00 kg of U-235 releases 8.21e13 J. https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-3/pages/10-5-fission

sources.nasa-iss-atcs: NASA and Boeing, International Space Station Active Thermal Control System overview: 70 kW rejected (35 kW per loop), ammonia supply 2.8 C. https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/473486main_iss_atcs_overview.pdf

sources.nasa-std-3001-v1: NASA-STD-3001 Volume 1 revision C 2023, requirement V1 4030: career effective dose below 600 mSv. https://standards.nasa.gov/
